title: stv-watch event line
description: One line of `stv-watch --json` output and of a session's events.jsonl. Field order is as listed: t_utc, t_local (only with --tz), type, steamid64, nick, text, then the extra fields of the type. Which extra fields each type carries is listed in docs/session-files.md and enforced here: `allOf` names the fields a type always has, `dependentSchemas` the types a field may appear on, `dependentRequired` the fields that come together.

t_utc.description: UTC time of the event on the recording's clock (live, the receive time), millisecond precision: of the packet that carried it; talk: the utterance's first frame (a later piece of a monologue: the cut that starts it); voice: when the utterance closed. Lines are in the order of t_utc, in a file and on --json alike. Lines a replay writes before its first record take that record's time.

t_local.description: The same moment in the --tz zone, to the second, without an offset. Present only when --tz was given.

type.description: talk: a player starts an utterance (or a piece of a monologue); voice: its end and what was said, the same utt. Game events: chat, console, connect, join, leave, death, team, name, server, sourcemod (filtered by --events). The viewer's own lines: conn (connection), net (traffic), play (replay), tvd (network client log), asr (a recognizer loaded or failed, the live one too), rotate (--rotate or a restart under --keep-trying: the last line of a session, naming the next, and the first line of the next, naming it), wait (--keep-trying: refused or the network client died, the next attempt is due at next_try_utc), done (exit, always the last line).

steamid64.description: SteamID64 of the player the line is about (the killer for a death), 0 when unknown or not a player.

nick.description: The player's nick as the stream names him; 'Console' for console lines; empty when none.

text.description: What happened, as text. For chat and voice: what was said (voice: empty when there is no text, see result).

channel.description: chat: the game's channel, its chat format name in lower case (all, team, alldead, team_dead, allspec, spec; tf2 also coach), plugin (a plugin formatted the line), saytext (SayText from a player).

ent.description: chat: entity index of the speaker.

location.description: chat, tf2 team chat: where the speaker was, as the map names the place.

userid.description: connect, leave, death, team, name: server userid of the player (the victim for a death).

networkid.description: leave: the network id as the server reports it (SteamID text or BOT).

bot.description: leave: the player was a bot. talk, voice: the voice came from the slot of a bot (SourceTV or a bot: a fake client, no Steam account to check), always true; nick is the slot's, steamid64 the one the server signed the voice with, and voice has no verified.

attacker.description: death: server userid of the attacker, 0 for the world.

victim.description: death by another player: the victim's nick.

victim_steamid64.description: death by another player: the victim's SteamID64, 0 when unknown.

assister.description: death, tf2: server userid of the player credited with the assist.

assister_steamid64.description: death, tf2: the assister's SteamID64, 0 when unknown.

custom.description: death, tf2: how, when the game names it: headshot, backstab.

feign.description: death, tf2: a faked death (Dead Ringer); the victim lives.

team.description: team: new team number (0 unassigned, 1 spectator; hl2dm 2 combine, 3 rebels; tf2 2 red, 3 blu).

via.description: server, sourcemod: the message that carried the text (TextMsg, HudMsg, SayText2, server_cvar).

dest.description: server via TextMsg: HUD destination code.

cvar.description: server via server_cvar: the console variable.

value.description: server via server_cvar: its new value.

seq_from.description: net, --debug only: highest sequence number before the gap.

seq_to.description: net, --debug only: sequence number after the gap.

lost.description: net, --debug only: sequence numbers lost in the gap (not declared choked).

result.description: voice: text (text holds what was recognized), no speech (the voice activity gate found less speech than --min-speech-ms, or the model heard none), asr off (no --asr), not recognized before exit (still queued when the exit stopped waiting, see --drain-ms), not recognized, queue full (live only: 600 s of audio was already waiting for the recognizer), recognition failed (the engine raised an error on it).

utt.description: talk, voice: the utterance's number in the run; a talk line and the one voice line of the same utterance share it (across rotated sessions too).

start_utc.description: talk, voice: the utterance's first frame (a later piece of a monologue: where the piece before it ends), the format of t_utc.

end_utc.description: voice: where the utterance's audio ends: its close, or for a monologue piece the pause it was cut at (the next piece's start_utc), the format of t_utc.

continued.description: talk, voice: a piece of a monologue after the first (cut at --max-utt-ms).

spectator.description: voice: the speaker is a spectator and sv_alltalk is off, so the players in game did not hear him.

details.description: voice: transport numbers of the utterance (audio and arrival seconds, Opus frames, concealed and silence-filled frames, bit rate, key presses, voice messages, share in split packets, arrivals, how long after the last frame it closed) and, with --asr, recognition seconds and the lag behind the speech.

speech_ms.description: voice: milliseconds of speech Silero VAD found in the utterance (32 ms windows above 0.5); only when the recognizer looked at it.

slot.description: talk: the server slot (svc_VoiceData from_client) of the voice message that started it. voice: the server slot (svc_VoiceData from_client) the utterance's voice messages came from; with a mismatch, the slot of the first one that did not match.

verified.description: voice: whether the server's userinfo entry for the slot names the player whose SteamID the voice payload carries (steamid64): true when every voice message that could be checked matched, false when any did not (see slot_steamid64), null when none could be checked (no userinfo table yet, or an empty slot). Absent when the voice came from a bot's slot (see bot).

slot_steamid64.description: voice, only when verified is false: SteamID64 of the player the server had in that slot (0 for one without an account).

next_dir.description: rotate, the last line of a session: the absolute path of the session directory the run goes on in.

next_events.description: rotate, the last line of a session: the absolute path of the next session's events.jsonl, to go on reading there.

prev_dir.description: rotate, the first line of a rotated session: the absolute path of the session directory before it.

prev_events.description: rotate, the first line of a rotated session: the absolute path of the previous session's events.jsonl.

reason.description: rotate: restart when a new network client starts after a --keep-trying wait (its journal and files go in a directory of their own); absent for the --rotate schedule.

quit.description: done and wait: what ended the run or the attempt, the label meta.json has as quit: key q, SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP, time limit, client left: time limit, end of recording, precheck, alarm, client died (rc N), asr failed, password, write error, crash.

class.description: done and wait: the class of the ending, one per exit code: ok 0, bug 1, usage 2, refused 3, client 4, io 5.

cause.description: done and wait: why, as text: the relay's refusal, how the network client died, the exception of a bug, the file that could not be written; empty when the run ended as asked.

rc.description: done: the exit code of the run.

retrying.description: done: false (the run ends); wait: true.

tvdump_rc.description: done: the exit code of the last network client; null when none ran or it had to be killed.

attempt.description: wait: the number of the attempt that failed, 1 for the first.

next_try_utc.description: wait: when the next attempt is due, the format of t_utc; it comes earlier when the password file changes.

version.description: Only on the first line of a session (asr when --asr loads the recognizer first, else conn live, play replay and follow, done if the run ended before either; rotate in a session a rotation opened): the stv-watch version that wrote it, as `stv-watch --version` names it: 0.1.0 or, run from a git checkout, 0.1.0+g976b9ae (.dirty when tracked files differ from the commit).
